title: Schengen visa
tagline: Visas to Germany, France, Italy, Spain and other Schengen countries.

facts.label: Where to apply
facts.value: Bishkek or Almaty — depends on the country

intro:
A Schengen visa opens 29 European countries. You apply to the consulate of your main destination — and each country has its own requirements, visa centre and booking times.

We tell you where to apply, assemble the documents, complete the form, arrange hotel bookings and insurance, and book your biometrics appointment.
services: Choosing the right country and visa type
Itinerary, hotel and flight reservations for the visa
Booking the visa centre or consulate appointment

sections.heading: Which country to apply to
sections.body:
Apply to the country where you will spend the most days. If the days are split evenly, apply to the country of first entry. Choosing the wrong country is a frequent reason for refusal.

Some countries accept applications from Kyrgyz citizens in Bishkek, others only in Almaty or through another country’s mission. We will confirm the current procedure for yours.

sections.heading: National D visa
sections.body: Study, work or a long stay require a national visa of a specific country rather than a Schengen visa. The requirements are stricter — we help assemble documents for studying in Italy and France.

documents: Passport issued within the last 10 years and valid 3 months beyond the trip
Medical insurance for the whole trip
Invitation — for visitor and business visas
documents_note: Requirements differ by country — we give you the exact list for yours.

faq.q: How long does a Schengen visa take?
faq.a: Usually about 15 calendar days, longer in peak season. Apply early — appointments can be booked several months before the trip.

faq.q: Do I need my own income?
faq.a: You must show you can afford the trip. If you are not working, a relative can sponsor you — we explain how to do it properly.

faq.q: Can I get a multiple-entry visa?
faq.a: Yes. With a good travel history, consulates more often issue multiple-entry visas for longer periods.
